subject: Re: Capacity & isolation needs — post-call recap and proposed reservations
messages:
From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medstack.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Capacity & isolation needs — post-call recap and proposed reservations

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured what I heard below; please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain and goals
- Production inference latency variability during peak traffic (esp. morning batch + realtime queries). Current p95 for your reranking model spikes to ~700–900ms.
- Compliance requirement: tenant isolation for PHI-adjacent workflows (customer data must never touch multi-tenant KV cache).
- Predictability for month-to-month spend; procurement prefers a reserved commitment vs burst-on-demand.

Proposed Redwood reserved footprint (opinionated):
- Base reserved pool: 6x A100-like GPUs (steady-state) to cover peak concurrent streams with smart batching + KV prefix caching.
- Isolation: dedicated "silo" pool for PHI paths — separate instance family + disabled cross-tenant cache; expected 1–2 GPUs initially, scale to 3 within 60d if utilization >70%.
- Burst policy: allow up to 40% burst into shared capacity during business hours (soft cap) with automatic fallback to smaller model variant if capacity constrained.
- SLA targets we discussed: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; p95 inference latency SLO target 250–350ms for the primary generation path (rarer rerank/long context flows will be higher).

Estimated rollout timeline (high level)
- Week 0–2: procurement & contract (SLA + isolation addendum).
- Week 3–4: private pool provisioning + initial model profiling (we'll run a short perf job with your representative prompt set).
- Week 5–6: staging cutover (canary on 10% traffic) + monitoring/trace hooks.
- Week 8: production traffic shift and final tuning.

Open questions / asks for you
1) Can you confirm the steady-state concurrent streams target (we heard ~180 qps across 3 regions) — that will validate the 6-GPU recommendation.
2) Who is the procurement contact to run the reserved capacity PO?
3) Do you have a list of representative prompt sets for the reranker+generator (we'll need ~300 sample requests for profiling).

Attachments: I attached a short capacity plan and an SLA draft for your legal team to scan.

Next steps
- I'll follow up with a formal quote and a one-page reserved capacity SOW by EOB tomorrow.
- If this looks good, we can loop in our solutions engineer (Marissa) for profiling sessions next week.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Kim Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medstack.com>
To: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@medstack.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Capacity & isolation needs — post-call recap and proposed reservations

Kim — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed and is a helpful way to show the options. A few quick clarifications: 

- Concurrent streams: our product team confirmed ~160–200 qps is accurate during peak (US west + central).
- For the PHI flows we currently have ~10% of total traffic, so your 1–2 GPU silo starting point sounds reasonable.
- Pricing: can you give a rough monthly committed cost range (ballpark) for the 6x reserved + 1–2 GPU silo so we can brief procurement?

Procurement contact: please loop in Maya Rao (maya.rao@medstack.com) — she handles reserved infrastructure and contracts.

Also attaching a small anonymized sample of the reranker requests (we redacted PHI) — hopefully useful for profiling.

Alex
CTO, MedStack
From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medstack.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@medstack.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Capacity & isolation needs — post-call recap and proposed reservations

Alex — great, thank you for the confirmations and the sample prompt set. Ballpark committed cost (high level, subject to final model/quantization choices):
- 6x reserved GPUs (steady pool): $28k–$34k / month committed (includes reserved capacity discount, networking).
- Isolation silo (1–2 GPUs reserved): $6k–$10k / month reserved depending on exact instance type and KC cache isolation mode.
- One-time onboarding/profiling professional services (optional): $8k (2 days of SE time) — covers model profiling, perf tuning and tracing hooks.

Notes on SLA & tech tradeoffs
- 99.9% reserved pool availability SLA will include a defined remediation credit table in the SOW; we'll tie latency SLOs to the profiling job results and a small SLA ramp during the first 30d.
- For strict PHI isolation we recommend a dedicated pool + disabled cross-tenant cache; this increases per-token cost ~8–12% but eliminates noisy-neighbor cache risks.

Immediate next steps
1) I'll send a short quote + SOW + the capacity plan (attached) by EOB today.
2) Kim/Marissa/SE team to schedule a 90-minute profiling session next Tue or Wed (please confirm preferred day/time).
3) Once you confirm procurement contact (Maya), I'll open a HubSpot deal and attach the DocuSign SOW for signature.

Attachments: MedStack_capacity_plan_v1.pdf, SLA-draft-99p9.docx

Thanks — I’ll get the quote into your inbox today.

Best,
Kim Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
